To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adsorption of organic compounds on biochars at high heat temperature can be described by Polanyi-based Dubinin-astakhov (DA model), and the adsorption capacity of biochars is determined by the pore-fitting mechanism with molecular sieves effect, and hydrophobicity, π-π bonding and hydrogen bonding are the main forces of adsorption, and these adsorption forces of biochars are determined by the aromaticity of biochars.

adsorption capacity of biochar is mainly affected by the pore-filting mechanism and the molecular sieving effect of biochar pores, and the adsorption affinity is mainly affected by hydrophobicity, π-π bonding and hydrogen-bond interaction of organic compounds.

adsorption capacity of biochars is mainly determined by the total pore volume, average diameter of microropre and molecular sieving effect, and that adsorption affinity of biochars for aromatic compounds is mainly determined by aromaticity and micropore volume of biochars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adsorption of organic pollutants onto biochars and the correlations of adsorption with biochar properties, which could provide the basis for biochar application as an adsorbent.
the correlations of the adsorption behavior and properties of biochars, providing a better understanding of the adsorption mechanisms of organic compounds on biochars.
the adsorption of aromatic compounds by high temperature pyrolyzed biochars from various biomasses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adsorption of aromatic compounds on high heat treatment treated biochars is dominated by pore filling mechanism and the main driving forces of adsorption are hydrophobic effect and π-π interaction.

the adsorption of organic compounds on biochars is dominated by pore filling and molecular sieving effect, with the hydrophobic effect and π-π interactions being the major forces responsible for the adsorption.

biochars with high aromaticity, large micropore volume and micropore diameter would be more effective for adsorbing organic compounds by the pore-filing mechanism with hydrophobic effect and π-π interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adsorption of organic compounds on biochars at high heat temperature (700 °C) is mainly captured by pore-filling mechanism, which is affected by molecular sieving effect of micropores in biochars.
the adsorption behavior is mainly governed by the physicochemical properties and the chemical structure of biochars, and the chemical structures of organic compounds.

the adsorption behavior and mechanism of organic compounds on biochars are determined by the physicochemical properties and chemical structure of biochars and the chemical structure of organic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

biochar with higher aromaticity has stronger π-π interaction with aromatic molecule and stronger hydrophobic effect with aromatic molecule, while the hydrogen-bonding strength between biochars and organic molecules is not correlated to biochars properties.

the adsorption of organic contaminants by biochars is a complex process, and it is not possible to predict their adsorption behavior using a single property of biochar or a single property of adsorbate.

the biochar produced from biomass with higher aromaticity, such as chitin, lignin and cellulose, have stronger adsorption capacity for aromatic compounds, while biochar produced from lignocellulosic biomass with higher H/C, such as rice straw, wood chips and bamboo chips, have higher adsorption affinity for aromatic compounds.
